newsitem.title: USA: Evacuees in Louisiana chlorine leak returning home.
newsitem.headline: Evacuees in Louisiana chlorine leak returning home.

text.p: Hazardous materials specialists capped a leaking chlorine tank early Thursday, allowing more than 600 evacuees to begin returning home, seven hours after the incident began, state police reported.

"It's all over now, and nobody was hurt," Louisiana State Police Master Trooper Howard McKee said. "The leak was stopped about midnight. We waited almost an hour to make sure it would hold and are letting people go home now."

The evacuees, including 150 nursing home residents, were ordered from their homes in this small, north-central Louisiana town about 6 p.m. Wednesday after a one-ton chlorine tank used to treat well water for drinking began to leak, authorities said.
McKee said the leak, between the tank and the shutoff valve, was sealed with a sleeve. A tank service company was called in to finish securing the tank and move it from town, he said.
